explanation: New Binary Detection -- an unrecognized process is running that wasn't present during the initial learning period. SPLIT OUT FROM rootkit_malware (2026-08-28) after definitively confirming, from real source, that Alert.xml's unknown_binary tag has nothing to do with rootkits. The real continuous detector is /athinio/bin/secOpsScript_112_bkp: a daemon that loops every 5 seconds enumerating every running PID's binary via readlink -f /proc/$pid/exe. For the first 2 weeks (1209600s) after first run, every distinct binary path seen is recorded into /athinio/system/unique_binaries.txt as the learning-phase baseline. After that, any running binary NOT in that baseline (and not in a couple of allow-list files) gets logged -- 'Attack : Unknown binary detected: <path> (PID N)' -- to /rationalVault/log/rationalclient.log and /var/log/osstatus.log, and sets alertlog.xml's Unknown_binary to 1, which rolls up to Alert.xml's unknown_binary. A separate wrapper, /athinio/bin/secOpsScript_112 (no _bkp suffix), manages the daemon (starts/stops it) and handles admin actions -- killing the offending process (kill_unknow_binary via param_cmd_112.xml) -- plus operator-triggered and automatic 24-hour ignore/reset (same self-clearing pattern as config_drift, gateway_breach_activity, and user_breach). This wrapper also writes secOpsOutput_112, but for the DETECTED case specifically it appends the real offending binary list ('Detected Unknown Binaries:' + the path(s)) -- unlike gateway_breach_activity/user_breach's purely-restated evidence, this one adds genuinely useful detail beyond the bare tag.

known_patterns.meaning: Unrecognized binary detected -- a running process's binary wasn't seen during the 2-week learning period. Confirmed live on real hierarchy 5/101/1/4/1 (2026-08-28): /usr/lib/systemd/systemd-user-runtime-dir.

metadata.caveat: SPLIT FROM rootkit_malware (2026-08-28): this entry now owns Alert.xml's unknown_binary tag exclusively -- rootkit_malware has been rebuilt around rkhunter's own evidence file (secOpsOutput_91) instead, since real source confirms rkhunter never touches this tag. A clean read during the first 2 weeks after deployment doesn't mean nothing unusual is running -- it means the baseline is still being built and nothing gets flagged yet, the same class of caveat as gateway_breach_activity's/user_breach's baseline periods.
